transcript: My grandfather is 84, he began to paint 10 years ago After retirement, he had time on his hands and wanted to focus on something In his youth he had been convinced that he had no talent for painting An art teacher in middle school told him you are bad at painting You are better suited for music since then he had not touched a brush But after retirement, he happened to stand before a painting in a museum, and thought he wanted to paint too. Already 74, the family worried that he was too old to begin, yet he joined a local painting class. People of various ages came to the class But he was the oldest, at first he was shy But he gradually found joy in it Ten years on, his works hang on the walls throughout the house. He has even held a small exhibition at a local gallery. His grandchildren treasure his paintings as their favorite. He says age has nothing to do with beginning something. Creation keeps a person young. My grandfather's hand, when he holds a brush, does not tremble The act of painting calms his nerves and sharpens his focus Art may be a powerful answer to the challenges of old age It is never too late to begin something My grandfather's example demonstrates this to me
